questions.question: D1 — Which implementation approach should this plan use? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-approach-selection>

options.label: A) Current plan as-is
options.description: Ship the handler as described: raw SQL fragment, inline email with no rescue, no new tests, N+1 order query. Smallest diff. Completeness: 3/10 — SQL injection is explicit in the plan text, email failures cause ambiguous HTTP 500 after payment commits.
options.preview:
APPROACH A: Current Plan
  Risk:    HIGH
  Pros:    - Smallest diff
           - Minimal new code
  Cons:    - SQL injection (plan explicitly states no sanitization)
           - Email exception after DB commit → HTTP 500
             → Stripe retries → dedup blocks → email silently lost
           - N+1 query on orders
           - Zero test coverage on payment path

options.label: B) Parameterized queries + email rescue + tests + batch query (recommended)
options.description: Same handler class, same existing contracts, but: (1) parameterized DB lookup eliminates SQL injection, (2) email failure caught and logged, not rethrown, (3) basic tests for happy path + edge cases, (4) batch order query. Completeness: 9/10.
options.preview:
APPROACH B: Correct Implementation
  Risk:    LOW
  Pros:    - Eliminates SQL injection entirely
           - Email failure becomes a warning, not a 500
           - Tests catch regressions before production
           - Batch query is correct under any load
  Cons:    - More LOC than Approach A
           - Requires decision on where to catch email exceptions
  Reuses:  All existing guards, DB client, mail client,
           parameterized query helpers

options.label: C) Approach B + async queue for email fan-out
options.description: Same as B but email goes through an async job queue. Handler returns HTTP 200 immediately after DB commit; email delivery is decoupled. Completeness: 10/10 — but larger scope, requires confirmed job infrastructure.
options.preview:
APPROACH C: Queue-Backed Notifications
  Risk:    MED (depends on existing job infrastructure)
  Pros:    - Email failure never affects webhook response code
           - Retry logic for email in the queue, not via Stripe replay
           - Most resilient long-term architecture
  Cons:    - Larger diff if no job system confirmed
           - Introduces at-least-once email delivery question
           - More moving parts to operate
